result:
If I could change the world in one way, I'd make people significantly less prone to self-deception.

Most of humanity's biggest problems aren't caused by a lack of resources, intelligence, or even goodwill. They're caused by people believing what they *want* to be true rather than what *is* true — and then building entire systems, movements, and personal lives around those comforting fictions. Politics, relationships, business, science, even how we raise our kids: so much of it runs on motivated reasoning, status games, and narrative protection.

If people were meaningfully better at updating their beliefs when confronted with evidence — and worse at protecting their egos from uncomfortable realities — a huge number of downstream problems would become easier to solve. Not because humans would suddenly become perfect, but because the *rate* at which we recognize and correct our mistakes would improve. Bad ideas would die faster. Good ones would spread more easily. Coordination on hard problems (from AI alignment to governance to personal health) would get less poisoned by tribal signaling.

It's not as emotionally satisfying as "end poverty" or "make everyone kind," but those things are downstream of better thinking anyway. Fix the root epistemology problem, and you get leverage on everything else.
